items.title: Back-to-back days of dominance for the Tigers: Here are the highlights
items.summary: Tanzid Tamim starred with a spectacular century, perfectly supported by a crucial half-century from skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto.

items.title: 'That’s some turnaround': India's Ashwin hails Bangladesh
items.summary: Bangladesh have caught the cricketing world’s attention after dominating Australia through the first two days of their opening Test in Darwin.

items.title: ‘They’ll be nervous’: Ponting warns Australia as Bangladesh take control
items.summary: With Bangladesh 153 runs ahead and the pitch appearing easier for batting, Ponting believes the next phase could reveal plenty about the character and quality of Australia’s batting order.

items.title: ‘Kept calm and played to the merit of the ball’: How Tanzid made history in Darwin
items.summary: Bangladesh opener Tanzid Hasan kept his composure and played the ball on its merit to produce a history-making century in only his second Test, putting his side in a commanding position against Australia in Darwin on Friday.

items.title: Tanzid, Shanto and Mehidy keep Bangladesh in front after gripping day's play
items.summary: Australia had most of their success in a brief spell with the second new ball, but it's been Bangladesh most of the way otherwise

items.title: Sri Lanka name strong squad for Asia Cup title defence
items.summary: Sri Lanka are slotted in Group B alongside Bangladesh, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates for the Asia Cup. The defending champions will begin their campaign against the UAE on August 29.

items.title: Miraz, Mahmud show grit as Bangladesh end Day 2 with 153-run lead
items.summary: Mehidy Hasan Miraz remained unbeaten on 32 off 73 balls while Hasan Mahmud was not out on 13 off 76 deliveries as Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the first Test against Australia on Friday with 351 runs on the board, having lost six wickets.

items.title: Smith was ready to walk off before DRS flat line

items.title: Hasan shows Tigers have more than express pace
items.summary: If Australians did not know Hasan Mahmud before the first Test in Darwin, they certainly know the Bangladesh pacer now.

items.title: Mahmud's 6 for 55 gives Bangladesh dream start
items.summary: Steven Smith waged a lone battle for Australia with 71 in 109 balls, but it was largely a sorry batting effort

items.summary: Taijul Islam, who had picked up an injury while batting in the tour game and did not bowl at all, is expected to be fit in time for the first Test
